item.title: Ross Fire explodes to over 80,000 acres, forces evacuations in North Texas
item.description: The Ross wildfire has burned more than 80,000 acres across Palo Pinto and Jack counties, forcing evacuations, closing roads and disrupting schools.

item.title: Iran says Strait of Hormuz agreement with Oman puts ball back in U.S. court
item.description: As U.S. economic pressure bites, Iran touts a plan with Oman to get ships moving through the Strait of Hormuz and suggests the next move is Trump's.

item.title: Suspect arrested for allegedly killing influencer on livestream
item.description: Cesar Gastelum was dressed as a food delivery worker and taking part in a social media challenge along with two friends when he was shot dead.

item.title: During secretive trip, CIA chief warned Russia not to attack NATO
item.description: The purpose of CIA Director John Ratcliffe's visit to Moscow this week was to warn Russia not to attack NATO member states, people familiar with the matter said, amid U.S. assessments that Russia could try to test NATO.

item.title: Trump's oil and gas stock trades continued during Iran war, filings show
item.description: President Trump has accused oil companies like Chevron and ExxonMobil of "making too much money." He owns shares of both.

item.title: Deaths surge, 65 Americans among hundreds missing after Nepal floods
item.description: Hundreds of people, including many Americans, are still missing along the Nepal-China border after deadly floods and mudflows likely triggered by a glacial collapse.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy trial testimony ends, closing arguments set for Thursday
item.description: Testimony in Lindsay Clancy's trial is finished after jurors in the Massachusetts murder case heard from 85 witnesses.

item.title: Small plane crash into water near remote Alaska town kills all 4 on board
item.description: A small plane carrying four people crashed into shallow waters next to a remote coastal town in Alaska on Wednesday, killing everyone on board, officials said.

item.title: Scores killed, Americans among hundreds missing after Nepal, Tibet flash floods
item.description: The flash floods decimated villages, slamming into houses, roads, bridges and power plants.

item.title: Yayoi Kusama, groundbreaking artist known for her signature polka dots, dies at 97
item.description: The paintings, sculptures and museum installations of Yayoi Kusama, one of Japan's most respected contemporary artists, were widely exhibited around the world.

item.title: From 1985: "Rocky Horror" stars mark film's 10th anniversary
item.description: On Halloween 1985, Barry Bostwick and Richard O'Brien, stars of "The Rocky Horror Picture Show," joined CBS News to mark 10 years since the cult classic's release. Tim Curry, who portrayed the film's antagonist, Dr. Frank-N-Furter, died Tuesday at the age of 80.

item.title: Tim Curry, star of "The Rocky Horror Picture Show," dies at 80
item.description: Tim Curry was known for his iconic performances in cult classics like "The Rocky Horror Picture Show" and the original screen adaptation of Stephen King's "It."

item.title: Mom arrested for vandalism after breaking bus window to pull out child
item.description: A mother was arrested for vandalism in California after smashing a school bus window to haul out her own child. Carter Evans has the story.

item.title: New Mexico farmers, residents fear data center's impact on health, bills, jobs
item.description: CBS News reporter Riley Callanan traveled to New Mexico to see Project Jupiter, one of the country's biggest hyper-scale data centers, for herself. She spoke with residents and farmers about their fears, concerns and in some cases, hopes.

item.title: Nvidia's revenue and profits more than double in latest earnings report
item.description: Artificial intelligence juggernaut Nvidia blew past Wall Street's expectations for its latest quarterly earnings report, more than doubling its profits and revenue. Wall Street Journal tech reporter Robbie Whelan joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: FDA approves new pancreatic cancer drug that could extend patients' lives
item.description: Patients taking the first-of-a-kind pill, called daraxonrasib, lived for a median of 13.2 months compared with 6.7 months for chemotherapy recipients, studies showed.

item.title: Prince Harry and Meghan arrive back in U.K., BBC News reports
item.description: Prince Harry and Meghan, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, returned to the U.K. from California on Wednesday, six years after their tumultuous departure, the BBC reports.

item.title: How Dolly Parton donated millions of books to children
item.description: Late country superstar Dolly Parton helped millions of children develop a love of reading through her free Imagination Library program. Hardin Engelhardt, chief learning officer at Marbles Kids Museum in Raleigh, North Carolina, joins "The Daily Report" to discuss.

item.title: See which U.S. states are most at risk from Canadian tariffs
item.description: Canadian officials said the tariffs set to be imposed on more than 800 U.S. imports are "strategic" and designed to target some states.

item.title: Details on custody battle over Texas surrogacy baby
item.description: A couple from California confronted the surrogate who refused their request for an abortion for the first time Tuesday in a Texas courtroom. They argue she is trying to take away their biological child. Mark Strassmann reports.

item.title: Fans mourn Dolly Parton at Dollywood in Tennessee
item.description: Thousands buzzed into Dollywood on Wednesday, one day after Dolly Parton's family announced her death at 80 years old. Skyler Henry has more from the theme park she built.

item.title: NFL ends Pro Bowl after 75 years, will still honor roster at season's end
item.description: In a news release, the NFL said it plans to "elevate" Pro Bowl selections, with no replacement selections.

item.title: Pentagon upgrades awards of 3 Marines for actions after Abbey Gate attack
item.description: Five years after the attack in Afghanistan that killed 13 service members, the Pentagon upgraded the awards of three Marines who provided care in the wake of the blast.

item.title: Grand jury: DeSantis administration "misappropriated" $10 million
item.description: A Florida grand jury found the DeSantis administration misappropriated $10 million in taxpayer money for political purposes.

item.title: 8/26: CBS Evening News
item.description: Latest developments on Nepal flooding; Extreme heat fuels wildfires.

item.title: ICE arrests of people without criminal records hit record high, new data shows
item.description: The surge in arrests comes as the White House pushes ICE to hit a target of 2,000 per day.

item.title: Trump hasn't decided on Leavitt's replacement as press secretary, sources say
item.description: President Trump hasn't settled on a replacement for White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt, whose last day is Friday, according to administration officials close to the situation.

item.title: Highlighting Dolly Parton's philanthropy
item.description: Dolly Parton's philanthropic legacy rivals her musical one, especially with her book-gifting program, "Dolly Parton's Imagination Library." Adriana Diaz reports.

item.title: DOJ warns Kennedy Center could be knocked down if renovations blocked
item.description: The Trump administration said it may need to demolish the Kennedy Center if a plan to close the building for two years as part of a controversial renovation project pushed by President Trump and the organization's board is blocked.

item.title: Extended interview: Don Henley
item.description: Singer-songwriter Don Henley reflects on the Eagles' decades-long career, the larger than life legacy of his late bandmate Glenn Frey, and the emotional moment he saw Frey's son Deacon perform in his father's place. He also emphasizes the importance of connecting with fans, saying "music is medicine. And people need some medicine right now."
